I want to learn Real history. What books should I read?
Be wary. Anything with real in front of it is 9 times out 10, utter bullshit.

Also goes for anything recommended on the internet in a thread like this.

The real trouble is that by the time you get to the point of asking a question like "Where can I learn real history?" you're at the point where your idea of "real" probably involves serving some particular agenda. So even if you got a perfectly accurate history book you probably won't read it correctly.

Read lots of stuff, keep an open mind. Don't read books with obvious political agendas until you've already read a fair bit about the subject in question.

History books are written normally by the winners, people with agendas or some other point to make.

As suggested read as many as possible with varying point of views and try to piece together what your are interested in.

Oye, that's a big question. I suspect if you wished to stick with just books, you'd have to read thousands. Good luck with that.

I made this decision soon after university, when my brother recommended I listen to the School Sucks Podcast. Then, I sat down in front the internet for several hours every day for the past ~10 years. I asked the internet questions, and followed my nose, and still am. I take my time, absorbing as much information about every subject I have questions about and along the way find connections of other subjects I didn't think I needed to question, and many more subjects I didn't even know were there. Over and over again, I find that I am unlearning what I had been taught in school. I have also developed methods for identifying bullshit based on logic/reason, previously learned stuff, and by an examination of the information's sources. My perspectives on my findings have also changed and evolved along the way. Be objective, don't hold onto theories or stories too tightly, as you will no doubt find new (to you) information that will disprove what you think you already know. There is a lot of bullshit out there, so you will have to get good at sifting through it in order to find real truths.

The most important thing I've done though, is ask questions I would be afraid to ask other people, questions for which I would be shamed for asking. Basically I decided that I would consider even the most ridiculous questions and theories and use my powers of critical thinking combined with access to seemingly infinite information (thanks internet) to analyze them. Essentially, I became a conspiracy realist. I seek the truth. No matter how ridiculous the question or the answer, I figured there was a way to find enough information to decide on my own if it was confirmable, plausible, unlikely, complete bullshit, or unknowable. You have to remain objective though, I can't repeat this enough. Be objective. Check your emotions and your ego at the door or you will find yourself growing attached to theories and falsehoods, unable to let go when presented new information. If you think you already know something, find more sources to back it up, AND find sources that question what you know, compare the conflicting perspectives, and use reason. Think critically. If you remain objective and curious, you'll figure it out.

Some of the questions I've asked that led to very interesting answers:

What's the difference between Austrian economics and Keynsian economics? Which one is correct?

What really happened during, before, and after the communist revolution in Russia? How about in China?

How many Jews actually died in concentration camps? Were there actually gas chambers? If not, what does this mean?

What's the deal with Israel? How was it formed and why? Who controlled/occupied that land before it became Israel, and who was there before them, and who before them, and who before them?

Who really lived in the Americas first? Was it the so-called "Native Americans"? How far back do the records really go?

Were there really pox blankets?

Did anyone know the Japanese were going to attack Pearl Harbor ahead of time?

Were the nukes dropped on Japan necessary to end the war, or had the emperor already surrendered?

What's the connection between central banks and war?

What's the connection between central banks and Kennedy's assassination? What about other assassinations?

Did Jesus, or Mohammad even exist? If so, how do we know? If not, what does this mean?

Why are there large stone pyramids all over the planet? What do they have in common? What about other large ancient stone structures? What do we know about these ancient cultures, and what do they have in common?

How old is the Sphinx? What could this mean?

Who is Jordan Maxwell, or Eustace Mullins? Is what they say verifiable? If so, what does it mean? If not, then what is verifiable?

What is Maritime Law and how has it affected western civilizations?

Who burned the Library of Alexandria and why?

Were the moon landings fake, and if they weren't how could I know? If they weren't, is anything about them still suspicious?

How many UFO crashes are recorded in history? When was the first? Are any of these stories at all verifiable? If any UFO stories are verifiable, what do the verifiable sightings have in common?

*Who invented ______? Who funded this? What's the whole story?*

Why are people freaking out about weather modification?

What's up with the Bohemian Grove? Is it what some claim it to be? Why do people make these claims? Do they know something I don't? Who is believing lies and falsehoods?

When something big happens in the world, how is it reported on in other countries compared to how it is reported on in my country? Why is there a difference?

Are some of the Mars rover photos photoshopped? Why would this be?

Any question you have is a good question, no matter how crazy it may sound. I'm serious, ask every question without fear or shame or hesitation. If you really want to learn, you will need to keep a completely open mind. Just make sure you don't fall for the bullshit.

As you go, you will no doubt find that you have been lied to about many things. Ask yourself, why? Why was I lied to? Why were my teachers and parents and friends lied to? Who benefits from virtually all the people of world believing lies? Who spreads the lies? Can I follow the money?
